limitations: The original full C01-C12/P0-P7 objective remains active. No daily installation, commit, publication, microphone or provider use is performed by this checkpoint.

The old raw-clock-counter regression fails as expected. The current helper has nine passing tests, also run in each actual GTK frontend. Before-paint stamps have a monotonic per-GUI serial, separate native frame counter and clock/surface generation.

Signal bindings are disconnected and recreated with the actual mapped native clock. Missing first-map clocks are retried by the normal poll. Complete positive GDK timing remains required; no timer, map or unmap event is a retirement receipt.

A surface lease is recorded before body display and retained until actual retirement acknowledgement. A new native surface cannot clear an old surface obligation, even when its GDK object has been destroyed.

Four native adapter cases use two real GTK windows in one test process. The positive pair replaces actual GdkSurface and FrameClock after the old token retired, then obtains fresh retirement while the new raw counter is below the old counter. The negative pair destroys a surface with a possible body and correctly remains blocked. This is not full terminal application multiwindow acceptance or a trusted destruction certificate.

Eight focused full-application cases comprise actual Block/VTE delayed presentation and same-XID unmap/remap. The remap cases retain native GUI, original jsh/PTY, exact token retirement and restored input identity.

All 84 existing GTK lifecycle cases and ten pending-launch cases pass with the current production binaries. Total current full-terminal native cases are 102; four separate native adapter cases are not counted as terminal application coverage.

The current 8-GUI/32-PTY matrix passes with at least two additional real GTK GUI descendants observed during body admission. Startup pane routing is completed before concurrent load. No P7 timing claim is made.
The whole HostGate/SharedHost source remains byte-identical to the previous checkpoint in all five copies. Ember/Frost production inputs are unchanged and their previous exact binaries are reused.

Two early native adapter harness diagnostics (ambiguous window search, final-exit observation) and initial compile/lint diagnostics remain preserved. Successful intermediate fixture runs do not substitute for the final-source cases.

Current JWM worktree changes made outside this phase are preserved by patches against the original archive base. The retained tested JWM binary remains separately identified; unrelated Eva/media work is not accepted by these tests.

Remaining requirements include broader terminal multiwindow and suspend scenarios, remote/detached/error behavior, real IME/memory/approval/voice/provider/API, trusted C11, P7 performance and reproducible installation/release.
